text:
A: Hi. Erm, hello. Can you hear me okay?
B: Yeah, fine. Hi.
A: Hi. Sorry, I'm Bethany.
B: Craig.
A: ...
B: So. Three minutes, yeah?
A: Yeah, I think so. I wasn't sure if we're meant to talk about anything in particular.
B: Don't think so. Just chat, I reckon. How'd you get on with the puzzle thing?
A: Erm, not very well, to be honest. I got stuck on the one with the shapes, the rotating ones, and sort of gave up on it in the end.
B: Yeah, that one was a bit daft. I just guessed most of them.
A: Oh, that makes me feel a bit better, thanks.
B: Where are you, then?
A: Bridgwater. In Somerset.
B: Right. Never been. Stevenage, me.
A: Oh, okay. Is that near London?
B: Sort of. Half an hour on the train. It's fine, yeah. Nothing much there.
A: What do you do? If that's... sorry, if that's okay to ask.
B: Yeah, course. Software developer. Back-end stuff, for a logistics company. Basically we write the systems warehouses use, so stock, picking, which lorry goes where, that sort of thing. I mostly work from home, so it's me in the box room all day with the headphones on. Pretty boring to explain, honestly.
A: No, that's quite interesting actually. My boyfriend works in a warehouse. He drives a forklift at a distribution centre off the M5. They've got a system that tells him where to go on a little screen, I think.
B: Yeah, that'll be something like ours. Probably not ours, but similar. Does he moan about it?
A: Erm... a bit. He says it freezes sometimes and they all just have to stand around.
B: Yeah, that's usually somebody on the back end. Could be me, to be fair.
A: I won't tell him.
B: Cheers. What about you, what do you do?
A: Erm, I'm sort of... I'm looking for work at the moment. I did a packing job but it was seasonal, so it ended. I volunteer at a charity shop two mornings a week, the hospice one. So, yeah.
B: Fair enough.
A: ...
B: Is that your drawing behind you? The bird.
A: Oh, yeah. It's a robin. I draw quite a lot, mostly birds and plants. There's a little egret that's been down by the river this week, so I've been trying to get that, but they don't keep still. They stand dead still for ages and then just go, and you've only got half a leg.
B: Half a leg. Yeah, that robin's decent though. Looks proper.
A: Thank you. That's kind.
B: You sell them or anything?
A: No, not really. I put some on Instagram. I've got a few hundred followers, which isn't much. I'd like to do commissions maybe, one day, but I'm not sure I'm good enough yet.
B: Few hundred's more than I've got. I'd just charge people. Honestly, half of getting paid is just asking for it. I've moved jobs twice 'cause I asked for more money and they said no.
A: I think I'd be too scared to ask.
B: Yeah, most people are. That's why they don't get it.
A: Mm. Maybe. Is that a bike behind you? In the corner.
B: Yeah. Road bike. Bought it in lockdown, cost way too much. I ride it about four times a year. Needs a service, I've been saying that for about a year.
A: We walk mostly. On the Levels, and up the Quantocks sometimes if Kieran drives us.
B: Is that hills?
A: Yeah, sort of... they're not huge, but it's really nice at the top. You can see right over to Wales on a clear day.
B: I'd probably cycle it if it was flat.
A: The Levels are flat. Very flat. That's kind of the whole point of them.
B: Go on then, maybe I'll stick the bike on the—
